page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-4800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, this x86_64 architecture system includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 4800 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong processing capabilities, with both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU performance scoring in the top 25%. Passmark CPU tests align with this, registering a score of 51801.15 and a physics test score of 8416.73, both placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is highly competitive for large-scale operations, with uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 488.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 225.61 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Conversely, small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth and Passmark database operations perform within the average middle 50% range.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is driven by its high resource density, combining substantial dedicated AMD EPYC compute power with a large 192.0 GB memory footprint and a generous 4800 GB NVMe SSD. This configuration avoids the need for separate network-attached storage, optimizing resource-per-dollar tradeoffs for data-heavy workloads. Given the strong multi-core CPU performance and top-tier large-block memory bandwidth, this server is well-suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and moderate-scale web serving or local LLM inference.
